The immigrant population since 1994

Foreign-born residents each March from the Current Population Survey, the most recent official count. Click a legend entry to show or hide a series.

Immigrants living in the United States, 1994–2025

    Show these numbers as a table

    Last updated October 7, 2026. American Community Survey 2020–2024 five-year estimates: 51 states, 925 metro and micro areas and 2462 PUMAs.

    Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates. "Immigrants" are the foreign-born: everyone who was not a U.S. citizen at birth, whether now naturalized or not, and regardless of legal status. Figures are survey estimates averaged over five years; small areas carry sampling error, so treat differences of a few points with care. Public Use Microdata Areas (PUMAs) are Census-drawn areas of about 100,000 residents on 2020 boundaries. Boundaries are drawn live from the Census Bureau's TIGERweb service.

    Birthplace layers and the 1994–2025 trend are aggregated from IPUMS USA (ACS 2020–2024 five-year) and IPUMS CPS (March supplement) microdata by tools/extract_microdata.py; see the groups page for citations.

    Tables used (ACS summary file, 2024 5-year): B05002 nativity, citizenship and region of birth; B05005 period of entry; B16005 English ability; B06009 educational attainment; B06012 poverty; B06011 median income. Boundaries: Census Bureau TIGERweb.

    Compiled by Daniel Di Martino. Fiscal years run October to September.
